P3: 36 reader-facing defect(s) stand in the final review — likely inside frozen environments or structural (placement/merge), needing operator adjudication or a P1 re-entry: • Internal pipeline identifiers leak into reader-facing prose: "a \leanref{S-1}{real-outcome observational experiment with a finite discrete confounder}", "a \leanref{S-2}{binary-outcome discrete-confounder experiment}", and "the \leanref{P-10}{residual shrinking-radius wedge}". Strip the S-1/S-2/P-10 anchors or render them as plain text. • Seven environments carry placeholder labels instead of meaningful ids: `\begin{definitionv}{synth_1}` through `{synth_7}` ("Binary exact-homogeneity source target", "Binary source law classes", "Fixed-sample binary homogeneous experiment", "Affine binary-to-real embedding", "Radius-channel hard-family embedding", "Empirical arm-cell mean", "Mean-squared error"). Rename to `def:binary-source-target`, `def:binary-source-classes`, etc., and update every `\cref{obj:synth_k}`. • Label prefixes contradict environment kinds: `\begin{propositionv}{thm:published-binary-collision-comparison}` and `\begin{propositionv}{prop:endpoint-reductions-all-d}` versus `\begin{remarkv}{oeq:shrinking-radius-frontier}` (the `oeq` prefix is a pipeline artifact). Normalize the id prefixes to the environment kinds. • Formalization jargon used as mathematics throughout. "Handle": "fix a polynomial handle \((N,\rho)\)", "Least-favorable handle", "handle-indexed heavy-light signed one-mark Chebyshev factorial estimator", "a polynomial calibration handle \(h=(N,\rho)\)". "Certificate/certifies": "The handle certifies that \(2\le K_n\)", "together with a transfer certificate with constants \(c_{\mathrm{rad}}\) and \(b_{\mathrm{rad}}\)", "the reciprocal approximation certificate", "The scalar budgets verified by the construction", "the arithmetic certificate", "The radial certificate asserted in the theorem". "Witness": "keeping the same ... witnesses", "as the approximate-homogeneity witness", "(Witness sequence.)". Replace with "calibration pair \((N,\rho)\)", "the calibration guarantees", "the transfer construction", "the required bound holds with the same data", "(Example sequence.)". • Type-theoretic vocabulary in the model-class discussion: "The law \(P\) carries an arm-cell outcome distribution for every arm ...", "a member of \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,2}\) carries all fields required for \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M}^{\mathrm{unr}}\); forgetting the homogeneity and radius fields leaves the same law", "the same consistency, exchangeability, overlap, mean-normalization, and second-moment witnesses". Rewrite in measure-theoretic language ("for each arm and cell, let \(\nu_{ak}\) denote the arm-cell outcome law, defined for all cells with the convention that zero-mass cells carry an arbitrary fixed law"). • Junk-value/totalization conventions from the formalization appear in statements and proofs: "For the endpoint \(n=0\), read the displayed algebraic rates with the totalized real-division convention \(x/0=0\)", "The case \(d=0\) is vacuous", "In the vacuous branch where the model index is empty, the real supremum convention gives \(\mathcal W_{n,d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}(\widehat\eta)=0\)", and the case-split constants in \cref{obj:lem:zeng-usable-occupancy-reciprocal} ("\(b_\epsilon:=c_\epsilon/8\) if \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(1\) otherwise"). Restrict the hypotheses to \(n,d\ge1\) and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\) and delete the junk branches. • \cref{obj:def:model-class} lists "\(0<\epsilon<1/2,\quad M\ge 1,\quad 0\le\sigma\le2\)" inside the brace defining a set of laws \(P\), so the display literally reads "\(P\) such that \(M\ge1\)". Move the index constraints out of the set-builder into the surrounding sentence ("For \(0<\epsilon<1/2\), \(M\ge1\), \(0\le\sigma\le2\), define ..."). Same fix for \cref{obj:def:unrestricted-class}. • \(\psi\) denotes two different functionals. \cref{obj:synth_1} sets \(\psi(P)=\frac1d\sum_k(\mu_{1k}-\mu_{0k})\), and \cref{obj:synth_3} repeats it, but Step 3 of the proof of \cref{obj:thm:radius-channel-converse} defines \(\psi(P):=\sum_k p_k\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)\) (the treated-arm weighted functional), and the proof of \cref{obj:thm:radius-channel-converse-all-d} uses the latter. Use distinct symbols, e.g. \(\psi^{\mathrm{ex}}\) and \(\psi^{\mathrm{rad}}\), and say which one each converse transports. • \(\tau(P)\) is applied to a binary law in \cref{obj:thm:published-binary-collision-comparison}: "every cell satisfies \(\left|\mu_{1k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\mu_{0k}^{\mathrm{bin}}(P)-\tau(P)\right|\le\sigma_{\mathrm{bin}}\)", but \cref{obj:def:ate-functional} defines \(\tau\) only for real-outcome laws. Introduce \(\tau^{\mathrm{bin}}(P):=\sum_k p_k(\mu^{\mathrm{bin}}_{1k}-\mu^{\mathrm{bin}}_{0k})\) explicitly. • In the same proposition, "write \(P_n\) for its \(n\)-sample product experiment and \(s\) for the published binary occupancy-weighted collision estimator" uses \(s\) for an estimator while \(s\) denotes a sample everywhere else ("\(\widehat\tau_n^{\star}(s)\in[-M,M]\) for every sample \(s\)"). Rename the estimator, e.g. \(T^{\mathrm{bin}}_n\). • \cref{obj:lem:same-cell-factorial-cross-moment} uses \(K\), \(j\), and \(r\) in its hypotheses ("\(j+2\le K\)", "\(r+2\le K\)", "\(4(K+2)^2\le m\)") and in its conclusion \(2(K+2)^2/m\), but the statement only introduces the order \(q\); \(K\), \(j\), \(r\) are never quantified. Add "let \(K\in\mathbb N\) and let \(j,r\ge0\)" to the preamble. • The magic constants in \cref{obj:def:polynomial-handle} are unexplained and reader-facing: "\(D_6:=8\log(27/4)\)", "\(\alpha_0:=\min\{1,1/(64\log 6),1/(512D_6)\}\)", the heavy threshold "\(256L\)", and "\(B:=4096L/m_1\)". Either name them as calibration constants fixed in the proof ("\(c_1L\)", "\(c_2L/m_1\)", with the numeric values recorded once in the appendix) or add one sentence saying which inequality each is chosen to satisfy. • \(N\) in the polynomial handle \((N,\rho)\) does nothing a reader can use: it appears only as the gate "the calibrated value is \(T_n^{\mathrm{poly}}=0\) when \(N>n\)", and every downstream statement re-derives it. Say plainly that \(N\) is a sample-size cutoff below which the estimator returns \(0\). • Vacuous clause: "Moreover, for the same constants and every such \(n,d,M,\sigma\), there are a capped alphabet size \(d_{\mathrm{rad}}\), a source family, a padding map into \(\{1,\ldots,d\}\), an embedding into \(\mathcal P_{d,\epsilon,M,\sigma}\), and a coupling realizing the radius-channel construction with source constant \(b_{\epsilon}^{\mathrm{rad}}\)" in \cref{obj:thm:radius-channel-converse-all-d}. The constant \(b_\epsilon^{\mathrm{rad}}\) never appears in any displayed inequality, so the existential asserts nothing checkable. Delete it and keep only the target-separation identity and the estimator-wise bound. • Tautological displays in \cref{obj:prop:endpoint-reductions-all-d}: the second display of the exact-homogeneity bullet is \(c\{n^{-1}+\min(1,d/n^2)\}\le n^{-1}+\min(1,d/n^2)\le C\{n^{-1}+\min(1,d/n^2)\}\), and the first display of the unrestricted-radius bullet is likewise \(cX\le X\le CX\). Both hold for any \(c\le1\le C\). Delete them; keep only the two displays with genuinely different sides. • \cref{obj:thm:published-binary-collision-comparison} assumes the published binary collision guarantee and then concludes that "the published binary collision guarantee above and the following algebraic comparison hold simultaneously"; the proof's Step 1 is "The assumed guarantee is exactly the first component of the simultaneous assertion." The hypothesis is never used to derive the two comparison bullets, which are pure algebra in \(u_{n,d}\) and \(h_{n,d,\sigma}\).
